failure_patterns.pattern: incomplete_result_persistence: Search or refinement results were not consistently bound and saved to cache, despite the skill already requiring both.

rejected_edits.content: - When a reply supplies information requested earlier, re-audit all still-pending requests across the full conversation and assess each domain independently; do not repeat completed work or let one domain's cache satisfy another. If the cache listing contains both base and refined results, prefer the most-refined compatible result that covers the still-valid earlier criteria, and apply only the new criteria. Copy cache keys exactly as shown in the listing.
rejected_edits.target: - Treat the latest user turn as an update to the trip plan. Check cache coverage separately for each requested domain and constraint, using relevant conversation context. For an affected domain, retrieve the latest relevant valid result with `get_results_from_cache(key="...")` into a local variable and pass it as `prior_results` when required. Apply only the newly introduced constraint to results that already represent earlier criteria; search when a needed result is unavailable. Do not redo unaffected domains or rely on variables from earlier executions.

rejected_edits.content: - When the assistant proposes a concrete domain, target, activity, or relation and the user affirmatively accepts, treat the proposal as an actionable request. Carry its details into the appropriate search or refinement using the relevant trip context; do not treat acceptance as a no-op or assume cached results cover it. Apply any additional constraint supplied in the reply as well.
rejected_edits.target: - Resolve elliptical latest turns against the immediately preceding assistant question and all still-pending user requests before deciding what action is needed. A direct answer can introduce a new destination, neighborhood, cuisine, amenity, or other criterion; it is not merely confirmation that an existing base result is adequate. If the answer names multiple locations, apply the other still-valid criteria independently to each location and create a distinct result for each.

rejected_edits.content: - For a one-sided threshold on a range field, preserve the stated boundary and use the opposite endpoint only when the schema documents it. For example, a restaurant rating of at least 3 on a documented 0–5 scale is `rating=[3, 5]`. For one-sided time limits, use the full schema-required range: “before T” runs from the earliest valid time through T, and “after T” from T through the latest valid time. Use documented endpoints and time formats; do not pass a scalar or invent bounds.
rejected_edits.target: - Validate value encoding as well as argument names. For fields documented as lower/upper endpoint lists, represent an exact requested value x as `[x, x]`; do not pass a scalar or singleton list, widen the value, or treat it as a minimum. Follow the schema for non-exact bounds and do not invent endpoints.
